newsitem.title: USA: Carolina bond elections on track despite storm.
newsitem.headline: Carolina bond elections on track despite storm.

text.p: Elections supervisors in North and South Carolina said Thursday they planned to proceed with weekend bond referendums despite the threat from Hurricane Fran.
Residents in South Carlina's Richland County School District 1 were scheduled to vote Saturday on a $184 million general obligtion bond issue for schools.

The inland county, which includes some of the urban Columbia area, is about 130 miles from the coast. County elections spokesman Mike Cinnamon said Columbia was expected to get heavy winds and rains late Thursday and Friday but the weather should allow the election to proceed Saturday.
Residents in Stokes County, N.C., were also scheduled to go to the polls on Saturday to vote on a $25 million general obligation bond issue for schools.

Stokes County Elections Supervisor Olivia Robbins said that county also should be able to resume normal operations in time for Saturday's referendum. The county seat in Danbury is about 25 miles north of Winston Salem, and is more than 200 miles from the coast.
The eye of Hurricane Fran was expected to come ashore early Friday morning near the North and South Carolina border, lashing the coastline with 115 mph winds.
